body:
FINAL REALTIME-AI SYNTHESIS

Recommended MVP architecture: upload worker (python-pptx + LibreOffice-rendered PDF/PyMuPDF; OCR/VLM only on failed/visual slides) -> canonical deck/slide/version records + cached context -> authoritative browser viewer emits slide events -> WebSocket audio to Korean streaming STT -> final transcript + current slide -> deterministic trigger + small structured-output LLM -> parallel internal hybrid search and external web search -> origin fetch/anchor -> deterministic field checks + compact verifier -> verdict -> Presenter Console approval -> audience card. Persist all transitions as immutable session events; Redis Streams consumers are idempotent; post-report recomputes from events rather than aggregating UI values.

Five-second recommendation budget, measured from utterance boundary/finalization trigger to Presenter Console (NOT presenter approval): STT endpoint/final 0.35/0.70s p50/p95; fusion+trigger+query 0.15/0.35; parallel internal/external retrieval 0.35/0.80; parallel origin fetch+parse 0.50/1.20; deterministic checks+compact verifier 0.45/1.10; rank/persist/push/render 0.10/0.25 = 1.9s p50, 4.4s allocated p95, 0.6s headroom. This is an engineering target, not a vendor guarantee. Enforce 4.4s cutoff, max 2-3 origin fetches, cancellation, caching of canonical sources, and abstain on timeout. Use partial STT only to precompute embeddings/query candidates; never publish from it.

Stack comparison:
A) Lean/recommended: web viewer + single API/orchestrator, Azure Speech or Deepgram, Postgres+pgvector+FTS+RLS, Redis Streams, Brave/Tavily, object storage. Fewest services, DB-enforced ACL, easy event/report joins; tune selective ANN.
B) Azure integrated: Azure Speech + AI Search hybrid/prefilter + Service Bus + Blob/Container Apps/OpenAI. Managed, documented Korean support; more cost/lock-in, and security-filter principal is NOT authentication.
C) Self-hosted: faster-whisper/live wrapper + Postgres/Qdrant/OpenSearch + NATS/Redis + local LLM. Best data control, but GPU/ops burden and no cited proof of Korean streaming latency; post-MVP unless offline is mandatory.

Verification contract: structured model output may propose `{claim, query, expected_fields}`, never URLs/ACL/slide IDs/numbers as truth. Fetch source yourself. Record `source_url, canonical_url, retrieved_at, published/effective date, content_hash, anchor, exact quote/table cell`; normalize and compare number/unit/date/entity deterministically before semantic support classification. Structured Outputs guarantees schema, not factuality; OpenAI itself says models may hallucinate and errors are worse than abstention: https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/structured-outputs and https://openai.com/index/why-language-models-hallucinate/ .

ACL/security invariants: authenticated server derives principals; DB/search prefilter before similarity; verifier and publication recheck ACL+revision+hash; audience payload must omit internal document name/path/quote even when presenter can access it. Use default-deny RLS: https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/ddl-rowsecurity.html . External fetcher needs SSRF controls (HTTP/S only, resolve/check every redirect, block private/link-local/metadata IPs, size/type/time caps, sandbox parsing): https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html . Treat fetched pages/internal docs as untrusted data, never instructions.

Caveats / unverifiable from vendor docs: (1) <=5s p95 end-to-end; must load-test. (2) Korean WER/number/entity accuracy and Korean-English code-switch behavior; run a target-corpus bake-off across Azure/Google/AWS/Deepgram. (3) Search API result freshness/primary-source recall. (4) LLM support-verdict precision. (5) a 10-person user study is not enough to claim market differentiation/generalization. (6) 'all sources original' is infeasible for blocked/paywalled/dynamic pages; UI should report unavailable origin, not use snippet as evidence. (7) C-05 auto-publication is incompatible with applicant p10 approval promise.

Core citations already sent: applicant PDF pp2-11,15; python-pptx, PyMuPDF, LibreOffice, Reveal.js; Azure/Google/AWS/Deepgram STT; Redis/NATS; Brave/Tavily; Azure hybrid + security trimming; pgvector/Postgres RLS; OWASP excessive agency; Kim 2018 Korean articulation-rate study.
summary: Five-second budget, stack recommendation, and unverifiable claims
